why: Design 9 with R1 centred, so a fall can end a run at once and a climb holds it longer, as B5's sign rule does. With R1 resting at 0.27 a fall could lower R2's c by at most 2.2 (8 x 0.27), about its window, so a run heading away waited for Q (~11 ticks) and lasted ~18 in the walk calculator; a climb was capped at ~48 ticks. R1's bias -1.81 -> -1.5 makes it rest at 0.5 (self 3: 3 x 0.5 - 1.5 = 0), its steepest point, where the loop gain is 0.75 (still monostable) and the swing is ~4x the input's: 8 (F - SL) of -0.5 drops R1 to ~0.1 (-3.2 on c: below the window's lower edge from Q's trigger level, so the run ends as the fall shows), and +0.5 lifts it to ~0.9 (+3.2: held until Q_out ~0.92, ~86 ticks at tau 100). R2's bias -3.09 -> -4.94 keeps c = -2.94 at Q's trigger (Q_out 0.25) with R1 at 0.5, so the rest rhythm is design 9's. Everything else is design 9's. Expected: in the walk calculator from 6,000 R, runs away ~5-10 ticks (design 9: 18), runs toward ~50-90 (38), and the crossing near B5's 0.7 h; in probes, steady light ~25-35% running at every level, ramps > 90%, falls < 10%. Watch-points: R1's noise is amplified ~4x at its centre, so in dim light noise will start and stop runs often (B5 does the same); the bright under-cancel (+0.3) lifts R1 to ~0.7 during bright runs (~44 ticks).
